clue.text: Prediction in favour of English players

parts.note: to be for something is to be in favour of it
the cast is the set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A pundit forecasts success for the English team selection.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast is a statement of what will happen, a synonym of prediction.

clue.text: Female expert's look

parts.note: an ace is a highly skilled person

explanation.surface: A description of the expression on a skilled woman's face.
explanation.definitionFit: Face can mean expression or appearance, as in 'a sad face', a synonym of look.

clue.text: Extremist spoke about capitalism, primarily

indicators.note: the word for a spoke goes around the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a radial is a spoke or line running out from a centre

indicators.note: only the opening letter of capitalism is taken

parts.note: its first letter, C

explanation.surface: A firebrand delivers a speech attacking capitalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' looks like the past tense of speak, but it is the noun: RADIAL, a spoke of a wheel, wrapped round C.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical holds extreme political views, so an extremist is a fair synonym.

clue.text: A scare as careless young man makes a dish

indicators.note: careless suggests the letters are handled sloppily and fall into a new order

parts.note: a lad is a boy or young man

explanation.surface: A clumsy young cook frightens people while preparing a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'careless' rearranges SCARE AS into CAESARS; the clue's opening A then sits before LAD to finish the salad.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caesar salad, of romaine lettuce, croutons and parmesan, is a well-known dish.

clue.text: Lying down in suite, finally, after drink

indicators.note: the pieces from 'in suite, finally' are placed following the word for drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink, usually in small mouthfuls

indicators.note: only the closing letter of suite is taken

parts.note: its last letter, E

explanation.surface: A hotel guest stretches out in their suite after a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Supine means lying flat on the back, face upwards.

clue.text: With last of deliveries, spinner's close

indicators.note: only the final letter of deliveries is taken

parts.note: its last letter, S
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a slow bowler finishes the day's play with his last balls.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, deliveries are balls bowled and a spinner is a slow bowler, but here the spinner is a child's top.
explanation.definitionFit: Close as a noun means an end or halt, which is what a stop is.

clue.text: Deal with, in theatre, a thespian

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of the following words

parts.note: the answer straddles the end of theatre, the a, and the start of thespian

explanation.surface: Handling an actor at the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat a matter or person is to handle or deal with them.

clue.text: Caught in rowdy punch-up after turning up for a tour of local hostelries

indicators.note: the brawl part follows the turned word
turning round makes the short word read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned

indicators.note: the cricket letter goes inside the word for a fight

parts.note: a brawl is a noisy, disorderly fight
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A night out drinking ends in a fight after arrivals turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses UP; 'in' puts C inside BRAWL. A 'local' is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub, so local hostelries are nearby pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub crawl is an outing visiting one pub after another, a tour of nearby drinking places.

clue.text: Scoundrel, for one, returned to scrounge

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man

indicators.note: returned means the short abbreviation is sent back, reading backwards

parts.note: e.g. (for example) means for one

explanation.surface: A rogue comes back to beg for things.
explanation.definitionFit: To cadge is to ask for something free, a synonym of scrounge.

clue.text: Saw senior scout formerly in lead

indicators.note: the scout goes inside the symbol for the metal

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
a Rover Scout was the old name for an older member of the Scout movement

explanation.surface: A veteran scout leader once sawed through lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb but is the noun meaning an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional saying or maxim, which is what a proverb is.

clue.text: What most shops do most days is obvious

definitions.text: What most shops do most days
definitions.meaning: first meaning: shops open and then shut each day

explanation.surface: A remark that shops keeping regular hours is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part reads the phrase literally, as a description of opening hours.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-and-shut case is one so clear it needs no debate, hence obvious.

clue.text: Bond character gets something in the post about a pyramid scheme?

definitions.text: something in the post about a pyramid scheme?

parts.note: a chain is a bond or fetter
a letter is a character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: James Bond receives a mysterious package in the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests the spy, but it is a chain that binds.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain letter asks each recipient to send copies on, a postal version of a pyramid scheme.

clue.text: Best in print, stylish

parts.note: a book that is out has been published and is in print
smart means neat and fashionable

explanation.surface: A magazine praising the most stylish thing in print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like the adjective but is the verb, to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to defeat or get the better of them, a synonym of outsmart.

clue.text: Except when included in gun lessons

indicators.note: the answer is contained within the letters of the following words

parts.note: the answer starts after the g of gun and runs into the second word

explanation.surface: A rule about when shooting lessons are excluded.
explanation.definitionFit: Unless means 'except if' or 'except when', introducing an exception.

clue.text: Local controversy in Cumbrian town

parts.note: in Britain a 'local' is one's neighbourhood pub, here a bar
a row is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: A local dispute is brewing in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like an adjective but is the British noun for a nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrow-in-Furness is a shipbuilding town in Cumbria, a county in north-west England.

clue.text: Communist measure demonstrates excessive bureaucracy

parts.note: red is the colour and nickname of communists
a tape measure, so tape is a measuring device

explanation.surface: A communist policy shows how heavy the state's paperwork has become.
explanation.definitionFit: Red tape is the idiom for rigid official rules and paperwork.

clue.text: Remarkable cue

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as an adjective, striking or notable
second meaning: a sign prompting action

explanation.definitionFit: Signal as adjective means outstanding (a signal success); as noun it is a sign to act, like a cue.

clue.text: Petty sergeant major everybody disliked

parts.note: SM is the military abbreviation for sergeant major
all means everyone
to have minded something is to have objected to it

explanation.surface: A trivial-minded sergeant major whom all the troops resented.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-minded means narrow and mean in outlook, a synonym of petty.

clue.text: Warning of danger from a member holding line

indicators.note: the pair of pieces holds the letter for line inside them

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A club member gives warning while keeping the line.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a signal or sound that alerts people to a threat.

clue.text: Nervous journalist, guy losing heart

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the crossword's usual journalist

indicators.note: the middle letter of guy is dropped

parts.note: the word itself before its centre goes

explanation.surface: A reporter feels anxious because a man has lost his nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means tense and on edge, a synonym of nervous.

clue.text: A group working in desert

parts.note: a band is a group of people or musicians
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A band of travellers at work out in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like the sandy noun but is the verb, to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon someone is to desert them, leaving them behind.

clue.text: Difficult to carry round store

indicators.note: the word for difficult carries the round letter inside it

parts.note: hard means difficult
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Something bulky is hard to carry around the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store' reads as a shop in the surface but is a stockpile.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a stockpile of saved goods, a sense of store as noun.

clue.text: Dull and unexciting team thrashed

indicators.note: thrashed suggests the letters are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: A sports report on a flat performance from a team that lost heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Tame describes something lacking spirit or excitement, so dull and flat.

clue.text: Insincere praise given prison reformer drinking coffee

indicators.note: the reformer's name takes the coffee inside it

parts.note: Elizabeth Fry was a 19th-century English prison reformer
a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: A campaigner for prisons is flattered over a cup of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: Elizabeth Fry appeared on the Bank of England five-pound note for her work reforming prisons.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattery is excessive, often insincere compliment-paying.
